'''''Persoonia stradbrokensis''''' is a species of flowering plant in the family [[Proteaceae]] and is [[Endemism|endemic]] to eastern Australia. It is an erect shrub or tree with hairy young branchlets, elliptic to egg-shaped leaves, and yellow flowers borne in groups of up to twenty on a [[Rachis#In botany|rachis]] up to {{cvt|100|mm}}, each flower with a leaf or scale leaf at its base.

==Description==
''Persoonia stradbrokensis'' is an erect shrub or tree that typically grows to a height of {{cvt|1–6|m}} with smooth bark above, rough bark on the lower trunk, and branchlets that are covered with greyish to light brown hairs when young. The leaves are broadly elliptical to egg-shaped, {{cvt|30–110|mm}} long, {{cvt|10–40|mm}} wide and hairy when young. The flowers are arranged in groups of up to twenty along a rachis up to {{cvt|100|mm}} long that continues to grow after flowering, each flower on a [[Pedicel (botany)|pedicel]] {{cvt|1–4|mm}} long with a leaf or scale leaf at its base. The [[tepal]]s are yellow and {{cvt|10–13|mm}} long. Flowering mainly occurs from December to May and the fruit is a [[drupe]].<ref name="ABRS">{{cite web |last1=Weston |first1=Peter H. |title=''Persoonia stradbrokensis'' |url=https://profiles.ala.org.au/opus/foa/profile/Persoonia%20stradbrokensis |publisher=Australian Biological Resources Study, Department of Agriculture, Water and the Environment: Canberra |access-date=7 November 2020}}</ref><ref name="RBGS">{{cite web |last1=Weston |first1=Peter H. |title=''Persoonia stradbrokensis'' |url=https://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=sp&name=Persoonia~stradbrokensis |publisher=Royal Botanic Garden Sydney |access-date=7 November 2020}}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
''Persoonia stradbrokensis'' was first formally described in 1921 by [[Karel Domin]] in ''[[Bibliotheca Botanica]]'' from specimens he collected on [[Stradbroke Island]] in 1910.<ref name=APNI>{{cite web|title=''Persoonia stradbrokensis''|url=https://id.biodiversity.org.au/instance/apni/549856|publisher=APNI|access-date=7 November 2020}}</ref><ref name="Domin">{{cite journal |last1=Domin |first1=Karel |title=Beitrage zur Flora und Pflanzengeographie Australiens. |journal=Bibliotheca Botanica |date=1921 |volume=22 |issue=89 |page=580 |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/181408#page/44/mode/1up |access-date=7 November 2020}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
This geebung grows from coastal heath to forest in near-coastal areas of Australia between [[Tin Can Bay]] in south-eastern Queensland and the [[Hastings River]] in north-eastern New South Wales.<ref name="ABRS" /><ref name="RBGS" />
